newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea Brent paper holds strong gains, wet quiet.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea Brent paper holds strong gains, wet quiet.

text.p: North Sea Brent CFDs and intermonth spreads on Thursday held onto strong gains made in the wake of Wednesday's late wet Brent deal, but physical activity was quiet, dealers said.
Brent CFDs for next week (Feb 24-28) were discussed at Apr Brent +38/40, some 20 cents above early Wednesday's levels. The following week (March 3-7) was pegged at Apr Brent +22/26.
"Everything has moved up but we haven't seen anything done yet," said one paper trader.
Brent intermonth spreads eased slightly in the morning, but were still talked some 10 to 15 cents up on early Wednesday.
Mar/Apr was at +45/50, having traded at +50 and +51 in the U.S. aftermarket. Apr/May was peged at +32/36.
Outright April Brent paper levels were trading down 10 cents at $20.53 a barrel at 1250 GMT.
A Brent cargo loading March 6-8 traded on Wednesday at March Brent -2 cents, a leap of some 20 cents on recent trades.
A single March 7-9 loader was passing through the paper chains on Thursday.
Norwegian grades were mixed, with Statfjord trading at firmer levels, but Oseberg seen heavily pressured.
Two Statfjords, both loading March 11-13, traded at dated Brent +40 and +45 cents respectively, up from the last traded level of dated +36 cents.
But Oseberg was under strain, having traded earlier in the week at a soft dated Brent +11 cents. Another cargo was traded into the Whitegate refinery in Ireland on Wednesday at a p+c price.
"Numbers on Oseberg vary wildly from dated evens to +20, it's pretty murky," a dealer said.
